newsitem.title: FRANCE: Eramet shares rise on N.Caledonia plan.
newsitem.headline: Eramet shares rise on N.Caledonia plan.

text.p: French nickel group Eramet rose sharply on Tuesday as investors welcomed news that a compromise had been reached over the re-allocation of nickel reserves in New Caledonia.
Eramet shares rose 6.05 percent to 276.8 francs at 1355 GMT.
News that a deal was in the pipeline eased investors' concern over political risk clouding Eramet's expansion in the French territory, dealers said.
"The market is welcoming news that an agreement is under way," one trader said.
In a statement Eramet said it had agreed to review a proposal to swap "on a fair basis" the mining titles of its Koniambo field with those of the Poum field.
The exchange would allow Canadian group Falconbridge and local Kanak independence groups to use the reserves from Koniambo to supply a nickel plant they want to build in the north of the country.

The French government, which is Eramet's main shareholder, supports the new project as part of its strategy to help rebalance the interest of local Kanak people with those of French settlers ahead of a vote on independence in 1998.
But investors initially worried that this would severely curtail the expansion of Eramet in New Caledonia.
Fears that Eramet might be forced to sell its strategic Thiebaghi mines in the north of the country drove the stock to a year-low of 221.2 francs on October 23.
Analysts welcomed the new proposal to swap the Poum and Koniambo fields because it spared the Thiebaghi reserves.
One analyst explained that Thiebaghi was crucial to Eramet's development as the company had already started developing the mine while production at Koniambo was not slated until the year 2010.
"It is excellent news for Eramet. It is just too bad that solution was not found earlier," one analyst said.

A source close to Eramet said the new proposal, if agreed by all parties, would allow the company to maintain its target to produce more than 60,000 tonnes of nickel by the year 2,000 from 1996 output of some 54,000 tonnes.
Analysts also said that it was still unclear if and when the new nickel plant would be built in the north as it required considerable funding.
They said the mine swap would take place only if the new plant was built.
